parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal entry/documents and facilities impose universal exposure: passport/visa marker rules, discrepancy/doubt can trigger refusal, evidence demands, possible permanent fraud inadmissibility; government-funded single-sex facilities are restricted. Immigration/corrections custody has documented forced labour, solitary, sexual abuse, conversion-therapy-style practices and birth-sex ward placement. The protective division’s public-accommodations law, hate-crime statute, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms and care shield reduce private-service and some care harms, especially for travelling families, but do not pre-empt federal screening, funded facilities or detention. Courts contest some orders; existing X passports remain valid and limited waivers exist. Net: high risk of administrative exclusion/stranding, with severe custodial consequences if an encounter escalates.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport/visa sex-marker rules: discrepancy, doubt about sex, or mismatched records can trigger refusal, evidence demands, or possible permanent fraud inadmissibility; passports reportedly confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded; allied advisories cite document risks.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; limited fraud waivers exist; ongoing civil-liberties litigation and a legal-aid passport guidance track current rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal border screening precedes state protections. A home-passport mismatch can become a refusal/fraud encounter; state marker self-determination does not offset entry rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopts conversion-therapy-style practices and removes hormones; one facility arrest involved men’s ward holding.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some orders are contested or enjoined; pretrial release occurred in a facility case; legal challenges exist, but no effective custody remedy is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State care and nondiscrimination shields do not cover federal immigration or corrections custody. A border or facility incident can escalate to birth-sex custodial placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; other jurisdictions have bathroom bans and criminal trespass; one arrest for a restroom was reported with handcuffing and jail ward placement.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Assessed division is protective: public-accommodations nondiscrimination, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, and no mapped state facility ban; private venues are more covered.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Division protections reduce private-venue harm but not federal, government-funded, or federally screened facility exposure. Facility conflicts can become police or immigration matters.

care_services.exposure: National rules threaten minors’ gender-affirming care, public funding, insurance reimbursement, school services, and health records; several proposals remain in litigation or pending.
care_services.protection: Division shield laws protect travellers seeking gender-affirming care and are recorded as enforceable against out-of-state action; insurer coverage and care nondiscrimination are documented locally.
care_services.interaction: Care shields mitigate state/local denial, especially for adult travellers and families seeking care, but federal screening, funding/school rules, and custody remain separate; shield provisions are not itemised.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises “radically pro-transgender” violent secular groups; a domestic terror reward memorandum names “radical gender ideology”; majorities support birth-sex documents and sports restrictions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime enhancement and panic-defence repeal exist; no documented enforcement data for these protections is provided.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises scrutiny where travellers are visible advocates, seek care, or fall into border/facility disputes. Division law moderates local policing but not federal posture.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders restrict minor care/social transition, threaten schools and funding, and can expose guardians to document scrutiny; a minor’s mismatched marker could raise border suspicion or fraud findings.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield laws protect care travel; school anti-bullying and transgender-student policies exist; local nondiscrimination and care coverage support guardians and minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Federal child-care and border rules operate alongside local shields. Travelling with a minor increases document friction, while care shields may limit state/local treatment denial.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No detailed division-specific street-violence data is provided, but hostile national climate, facility arrests, and public support for birth-sex documents suggest risk of confrontations and policing friction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State nondiscrimination, hate-crime law, panic-defence repeal, protective school/health policies may deter local harassment and support complaints.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Private-service harassment can be addressed locally, but police encounters may escalate if markers, documents, or facilities trigger law-enforcement or immigration attention.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Litigation leaves enforcement uneven; unknowns include which foreign documents border officers believe, ward placement during detention, minor-care conflicts, and shield-law scope; facility restrictions are expanding nationally.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, legal-aid FAQ, public-accommodations remedies, hate-crime enhancements, and recorded shield laws provide partial mitigation where protections remain operative.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies can reduce local harms but do not override federal screening, funded facilities, detention, or custody. Which rules apply at travel time remains uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest. Like the Visitor Conduct Register case, the dominant traveller harm is administrative exclusion, stranding, and document-based humiliation without credible execution. This case is slightly more severe because custody conversion/abuse, fraud bars, and counterterrorism framing are documented, though state care/privacy shields reduce everyday harms.

Above this anchor. That case features routine morality policing and arrests. Here the assessed division is protective and shield laws operate, but federal border/fraud exposure, custody abuse, and national facility restrictions remain heavy, keeping the case only moderately above the 0.25 morality-arrest pattern.

Below this anchor. That case involves universal database/registration friction without credible criminal escalation. This case adds permanent fraud inadmissibility risk, government-funded facility exclusion, and documented immigration/corrections harm, so federal custody and border consequences push it below the administrative-friction band.

parsed.synthesis: Risk is split by venue. In the protective division, private accommodations, healthcare travel and some school services are shielded; at crossings and in federally governed or government-funded settings, marker mismatch and doubt can trigger refusal, fraud findings, arrest, or custody. State protections reduce local service denial and care harm, especially for adults and travelling minors, but they do not pre-empt federal screening, funded facilities, immigration detention or corrections. After discovery, the likely consequence is exclusion/stranding with a credible severe custody path if an encounter escalates, placing the combined regime near the High/Elevated boundary.
